verdictRationale: The Writer closed the original privacy, trust, rollback, and taxonomy gaps, but introduced a new core automation contradiction. P3 requires approved migrations to run through autoapply, while the autoapply and executor rules still refuse REQUIRES_APPROVAL items even when approval artifacts are present.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A stable customer install has autonomous_apply true, a signed trusted manifest, and a valid install-bound approval token for a migration, but the autoapply job refuses to apply the migration because its PolicyDecision is REQUIRES_APPROVAL rather than AUTO_APPLY.
falsifiability.observableSignal: The run writes blocked.json or exits non-zero for the approved migration, and no migration marker appears under 06-runs-and-logs/updates/<ts>/migrations/<id>.json despite the approval token matching all required bindings.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Create a tmp customer root with autonomous_apply true, a trusted signed manifest containing one migration PlanItem, and a valid approval token matching migration_id, manifest_sha, install_id, risk_category, and expires_at. Run update.autoapply.job and assert whether the migration marker is written and decisions.json records the approval as satisfied.
falsifiability.threshold: PASS only if the approved migration applies exactly once and any missing or mismatched approval blocks the whole run

newIssueList.title: Approved migrations cannot autoapply
newIssueList.description: The spec now says P3 customer installs with autonomous_apply true apply an approved migration through the autoapply job. But the autoapply job is constrained so every PlanItem must evaluate to AUTO_APPLY, and any REQUIRES_APPROVAL refuses the whole apply. Risky migrations are defined to produce REQUIRES_APPROVAL unless approved, so a valid approval token still cannot satisfy the autoapply path as written.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define a separate terminal decision such as APPROVED_APPLY, or define PolicyDecision REQUIRES_APPROVAL as converting to AUTO_APPLY/SATISFIED_APPROVAL after exact approval binding validation. Then update autoapply and executor rules to allow only AUTO_APPLY plus approval-satisfied risky items, while still refusing missing or mismatched approvals.
newIssueList.lineRef: Architecture > Heartbeat vs apply; Deterministic policy evaluator; Apply executor; P3 exit criteria

ledgerReview.rationale: Heartbeat and apply are now structurally split, but the replacement autoapply path contradicts the approval-required migration path, so the original automation invariant is not fully satisfied.
Telemetry is explicitly default OFF, gated by both telemetry_enabled and heartbeat_url, and backed by a noop-adapter integration test.
The risky taxonomy now includes rules, instructions, skills, schemas, and behavior-driving registries with customer-default approval gates and CI classification linting.
TrustEvidence is explicit, untrusted manifests cannot apply on non-dev channels, and stable autoapply requires signing unless sha_pinned trust mode is explicitly elected.
Rollback now records absence tombstones and uses post-apply SHA checks before deleting update-created files, preserving local edits.
Approval artifacts now bind migration id, manifest SHA, target identity, risk category, expiry, and signature rules, with mismatch cases producing BLOCKED decisions.

preserveList.summary: The telemetry design is now enforceable because the noop adapter is wired unless both explicit policy keys are present.
The rollback model correctly handles additive files with absence tombstones and SHA-guarded deletion.
The PlanItem taxonomy treats behavior-driving text as risky rather than assuming only executable files can change system behavior.
